title: Emulating an OAuth Login for Playwright
subtitle: How emulate signs an end-to-end test in as a seeded user, with no real account
throughline: one Playwright click, from the sign-in button to a signed-in dashboard, logged in as a seeded user with no real Vercel account

chapters.title: Logging In Without an Account
chapters.blurb: Why e2e auth is hard, and how emulate runs the OAuth provider locally for CI.

story.title: Logging In Without an Account
story.subtitle: How emulate signs an end-to-end test in as a seeded user, with no real account

steps.title: Logging In Without an Account
steps.narration: End-to-end tests need a signed-in user — but real OAuth needs a real account. **emulate** runs the provider locally instead.
steps.say: End to end tests need a signed-in user, but real OAuth needs a real account. Emulate runs the provider locally instead.
steps.coverSubtitle: emulate runs the OAuth provider locally, so a test can sign in as a seeded user

steps.title: A real login, no real account
steps.narration: **Playwright** drives the **Next.js app** at `localhost:3000` through a genuine OAuth sign-in — but CI has no real Vercel account and no password to type.
steps.say: Our Playwright test drives a real browser through a real sign-in. The trouble is, in continuous integration there is no real Vercel account to log into, and no password to type.

steps.title: A drop-in provider on localhost
steps.narration: `npx emulate` boots a stateful **Vercel emulator** on `localhost:4000` with the real OAuth and user endpoints — *not mocks*. The app talks to it exactly as it would talk to Vercel.
steps.say: So emulate starts a local, drop-in Vercel provider on its own port. It speaks the real OAuth and user endpoints, so the app talks to it exactly as it would talk to Vercel.

steps.title: Deterministic seeded users
steps.narration: `emulate.config.yaml` seeds a fixed **users store** via `seedFromConfig` — the same known accounts on every run.
steps.say: The emulator is seeded from a config file with deterministic users. Every run starts from the same known accounts, so tests never depend on who happens to exist upstream.

steps.title: Nothing leaves the machine
steps.narration: Every request stays on `localhost`; nothing leaves the machine. That is what makes it safe for *CI* and *no-network sandboxes*.
steps.say: Because everything lives on localhost, there is no network call leaving the machine. That is what makes it safe for continuous integration and offline sandboxes.

steps.title: Sign in as a seeded user
steps.narration: The test signs in *as a seeded user* — no password, no real provider. To the app it looks like an ordinary OAuth login.
steps.say: The whole trick is this: Playwright will sign in as one of those seeded users, with no password and no real provider. To the app, it looks like an ordinary OAuth login.

steps.title: Following one click
steps.narration: We follow one click end to end: the **authorize redirect**, the **code and token** exchange, then the **session cookie** that makes it stick.
steps.say: Over the next chapters we will follow one click all the way to a signed-in dashboard: the authorize redirect, the code and token exchange, and the session cookie that makes it stick.

chapters.title: The Authorize Redirect
chapters.blurb: Clicking sign in redirects to the emulator's authorize page — a list of seeded users.

story.title: The Authorize Redirect
story.subtitle: How emulate signs an end-to-end test in as a seeded user, with no real account

steps.title: The Authorize Redirect
steps.narration: Clicking *Sign in* goes nowhere real. It redirects the browser to the emulator's **authorize** page — a simple list of seeded users.
steps.say: Clicking sign in goes nowhere real. It redirects the browser to the emulator's authorize page, a simple list of seeded users.
steps.coverSubtitle: the button redirects the browser to the emulator's authorize page

steps.title: The app's OAuth kickoff
steps.narration: Clicking the button calls the app's own **`/api/auth/[provider]`** route (`route.ts`) — its only job is to start the OAuth dance.
steps.say: When Playwright clicks the Vercel button, it hits the app's own auth route. That route's only job is to start the OAuth dance.

steps.title: Build the authorize URL
steps.narration: It builds the authorize URL with `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `scope`, `state` and `response_type=code`, then `redirect()`s the browser to `/oauth/authorize`.
steps.say: The route builds an authorize URL carrying the client id, the redirect URI, the scope and a random state, then redirects the browser to the emulator's authorize endpoint.

steps.title: Load every seeded user
steps.narration: On the emulator, `/oauth/authorize` calls `vs.users.all()` to load every seeded account from the store.
steps.say: On the emulator side, the authorize handler reads every seeded user from its store.

steps.title: One button per user
steps.narration: `renderUserButton` builds one button per user, each carrying hidden `redirect_uri`, `scope`, `state` and `client_id` fields — ready to post straight back.
steps.say: It turns each user into a button on a sign-in card. Every button hides the original OAuth fields, ready to be posted straight back.

steps.title: The whole login screen
steps.narration: The emulator returns the **user-picker** card to the browser. There is *no password box* — choosing a user is the whole authentication step.
steps.say: That card is the entire login screen. There is no password box; choosing a user is the whole authentication step.

steps.title: Pick the seeded user
steps.narration: Playwright finds the seeded user it wants and clicks. That form submit is where the real **code exchange** begins.
steps.say: So Playwright simply finds the seeded user it wants and clicks. That submit is where the real token exchange begins.

chapters.title: Code, Then Token
chapters.blurb: Picking a user mints a one-time code; the app trades it plus its secret for a bearer token.

story.title: Code, Then Token
story.subtitle: How emulate signs an end-to-end test in as a seeded user, with no real account

steps.title: Code, Then Token
steps.narration: Picking a user mints a one-time **code**. The app trades that code, plus its secret, for a real **bearer token**.
steps.say: Picking a user mints a one-time code. The app trades that code, plus its secret, for a real bearer token.
steps.coverSubtitle: a one-time code is exchanged, with the client secret, for a bearer token

steps.title: Submit the chosen user
steps.narration: The picker form POSTs `username` plus the carried OAuth fields to **`/oauth/authorize/callback`**.
steps.say: Clicking a seeded user posts the username, along with the carried OAuth fields, to the emulator's authorize callback.

steps.title: Mint and stash a code
steps.narration: It mints a random `code` and stores a `PendingCode` — `username`, `scope`, `redirectUri`, PKCE — in the `pendingCodes` map, with a ten-minute TTL.
steps.say: The callback generates a random authorization code and stashes the pending details, the username, scope, redirect URI and any code challenge, in a short-lived map that expires in ten minutes.

steps.title: Redirect back with the code
steps.narration: It `302`-redirects the browser back to the app's **`/api/auth/callback/[provider]`** with `?code=` and the original `state`.
steps.say: Then it redirects the browser back to the app's callback route, carrying that code and the original state in the query string.

steps.title: Exchange code for token
steps.narration: The app's callback POSTs `code`, `client_id` and `client_secret` to the emulator's **`/login/oauth/token`** endpoint.
steps.say: The app's callback never trusts the code on its own. It posts the code, its client id and client secret to the emulator's token endpoint.

steps.title: Verify everything
steps.narration: The endpoint checks the client secret with `constantTimeSecretEqual`, that the pending `code` exists and is unexpired, the `redirect_uri`, and **PKCE** (`code_verifier` vs `code_challenge`).
steps.say: The token endpoint verifies everything: the client secret in constant time, that the code exists and has not expired, that the redirect URI matches, and the proof key for code exchange, or P K C E, if one was used.

steps.title: Mint the bearer token
steps.narration: On success it mints a `vercel_…` token and registers it: `tokenMap.set(token, { login, id, scopes })`.
steps.say: Only then does it mint a bearer token and register it in the token map, tied to that user's login and scopes.

steps.title: Return the access token
steps.narration: It returns `{ access_token, token_type: "Bearer", scope }` to the app callback. The app now holds a credential standing in for the seeded user.
steps.say: The token comes back to the app in a standard access token response. Now the app holds a credential that stands in for the seeded user.

chapters.title: Becoming the User
chapters.blurb: The emulator resolves the token to a user; the app stores it in a session cookie.

story.title: Becoming the User
story.subtitle: How emulate signs an end-to-end test in as a seeded user, with no real account

steps.title: Becoming the User
steps.narration: A token alone is not a session. The emulator **resolves** it to a user, and the app bakes that into a **cookie**.
steps.say: A token alone is not a session. The emulator resolves it to a user, and the app bakes that into a cookie.
steps.coverSubtitle: the token is resolved to a user and baked into a session cookie

steps.title: Ask who the token is
steps.narration: The app calls userinfo with `Authorization: Bearer …`; every request first runs `app.use("*", authMiddleware(tokenMap))`.
steps.say: Holding the token, the app asks the emulator who it belongs to. Every request first runs through the emulator's auth middleware.

steps.title: Resolve the token
steps.narration: `authMiddleware` does `tokens.get(token)` and attaches the matching account to the request as `authUser`.
steps.say: The middleware looks the token up in the token map and attaches the matching account to the request as the authenticated user.

steps.title: Return the seeded profile
steps.narration: `/login/oauth/userinfo` reads `authUser` and returns the seeded profile — `{ sub, email, name, preferred_username }`.
steps.say: The userinfo route then reads that authenticated user and returns the seeded profile: the subject id, email, name and preferred username.

steps.title: Bake it into a cookie
steps.narration: `encodeSession` base64-encodes the `Session`, and the callback writes it to an HTTP-only `session` cookie.
steps.say: Back in the app, that profile and token are encoded into a session and written to an HTTP-only cookie.

steps.title: Render the signed-in user
steps.narration: `/dashboard` calls `getSession()` to read the cookie on the server, decode the session, and render the signed-in user.
steps.say: The dashboard page reads that cookie on the server, decodes the session, and renders the signed-in user.

steps.title: Assert a real session
steps.narration: Playwright asserts the **dashboard** shows the seeded user's name and email — a genuine logged-in session, *no real account*.
steps.say: Finally Playwright asserts the dashboard shows the seeded user's name and email. It is a genuine logged-in session, built entirely from a local provider.

chapters.title: The Whole Loop
chapters.blurb: One click, end to end: button, picker, code, token, cookie, dashboard — with no real account.

story.title: The Whole Loop
story.subtitle: How emulate signs an end-to-end test in as a seeded user, with no real account

steps.title: The Whole Loop
steps.narration: One click, end to end: button, picker, **code**, **token**, cookie, dashboard — a logged-in user with *no real account*.
steps.say: One click, end to end: button, picker, code, token, cookie, dashboard, a logged-in user with no real account.
steps.coverSubtitle: button, picker, code, token, cookie, dashboard — a logged-in user with no real account

steps.title: The test drives the app
steps.narration: **Playwright** drives the **Next.js app** through one full sign-in, just as a user would.
steps.say: Step back and watch the whole session. Playwright drives the app just as a user would.

steps.title: Pick a user, get a code
steps.narration: App → `/oauth/authorize` → pick a seeded user → a one-time `code` returns to the callback.
steps.say: The app redirects to the emulator's authorize page, and the test picks a seeded user, which comes back as a one-time code.

steps.title: Trade code for token
steps.narration: The app POSTs the `code` to `/login/oauth/token`; the emulator mints a bearer token into `tokenMap`.
steps.say: The app exchanges that code at the token endpoint, and the emulator mints a bearer token into its token map.

steps.title: Session, then dashboard
steps.narration: Resolved via `authMiddleware`, the session is cookie-stored and the **dashboard** renders the user.
steps.say: The app resolves that token to the seeded user and stores the session, then renders the dashboard.

steps.title: Assert the logged-in user
steps.narration: Playwright asserts the signed-in user — *no real Vercel account touched*.
steps.say: Playwright asserts the logged-in user, and the test has a real authenticated session without a single real credential.

steps.title: The full loop
steps.narration: **Recap:** click → picker → `code` → token → cookie → dashboard, all on `localhost`.
steps.say: Button to picker, code to token, token to cookie, cookie to dashboard. That is how emulate logs a Playwright test in as an OAuth user, entirely offline.
